entities.summary: James Alton McDivitt Jr. was an American test pilot, United States Air Force (USAF) pilot, aeronautical engineer, and NASA astronaut in the Gemini and Apollo programs. He joined the USAF in 1951 and flew 145 combat missions in the Korean War. In 1959, after graduating first in his class with a Bachelor of Science degree in Aeronautical Engineering from the University of Michigan through the U.S. Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) program, he qualified as a test pilot at the Air Force Experimental Flight Test Pilot School and Aerospace Research Pilot School, and joined the Manned Spacecraft Operations Branch.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a NASA astronaut in the Gemini and Apollo programs, McDivitt played a crucial role in the development of space exploration technology, contributing to the success of these historic missions. His experience as a test pilot and engineer helped pave the way for future human spaceflight.
